must_remember: Temporal coherence measures the phase correlation of electric field vectors $E(t)$ and $E(t + \tau)$ at the exact same spatial point.
Coherence time $\tau_c$ is inversely proportional to the spectral bandwidth $\Delta\nu$ ($\tau_c \approx 1 / \Delta\nu$).
Coherence length $L_c$ is given by $c\tau_c$ or $\lambda_0^2 / \Delta\lambda$, representing the spatial length of the wave train.
Interference fringes completely vanish when the optical path difference $\Delta x$ exceeds the coherence length $L_c$ of the optical source.
According to the Wiener-Khinchin theorem, the temporal coherence function and the power spectral density form a Fourier transform pair.

glossary.meaning: The degree of phase correlation of a light wave with itself at a later time at the same spatial point.
The maximum time interval over which a predictable phase relationship is maintained by an optical source.
The spatial length of a wave train over which temporal coherence is preserved, equal to $c\tau_c$.
A quantitative measure of the contrast of interference fringes defined by $(I_{max} - I_{min}) / (I_{max} + I_{min})$.
States that the power spectral density and the temporal coherence function of a stationary random process form a Fourier transform pair.
